sections.h2: Which office files a Darke County deed?
sections.html:
The Darke County Recorder does. The office is in the Greenville courthouse at 504 S. Broadway, answers at 937-547-7390, and keeps weekday hours of 8 to 4.

ORC Chapter 317 governs the office, which the county treats as its official keeper of records. Besides deeds and mortgages, the recorder takes mechanic liens, powers of attorney, recognizance bonds, IRS liens, corporate franchise liens and partnership papers. Its job is to record what you bring, so a deed drafted by you or your attorney has to be finished before it arrives.

sections.h2: What must be done to a deed before it is accepted
sections.html:
A deed needs the grantor's signature, an acknowledgment and the auditor's stamp before it goes to the recorder. ORC 5301.01 has the grantor acknowledge the signature in front of an authorized official (a judge or clerk of a court of record, county auditor, county engineer, notary public or mayor), who then certifies it.

The usual order in Darke County:

  1. Draft the deed using a legal description that fits the parcel. The county engineer keeps the tax maps and reviews deeds, land transfers and lot splits for proper boundary descriptions.
  2. Sign and acknowledge the deed.
  3. Take the deed and a conveyance fee statement to the Darke County Auditor on the courthouse first floor. The auditor's forms page lists DTE 100 for a standard conveyance, DTE 100EX for an exempt one, DTE 101 for homestead property and DTE 102 for farmland valued at its agricultural use.
  4. Pay the auditor the conveyance fee and any county transfer tax, get the stamp, and take the deed to the recorder.

Bring these to the auditor's counter:

  • The signed and acknowledged deed with its legal description
  • A completed conveyance fee statement on the right DTE form
  • Money for the conveyance fee and any county transfer tax

Splitting a lot off a larger parcel adds a step. Call the zoning inspector at 937-547-7381 with split questions. Building permits across the unincorporated area, Greenville and many villages go through the county building regulation office at 937-547-7379.

The schedule comes from ORC 317.32. Through page two, a standard deed or mortgage costs $17 plus an equal $17 housing trust fund fee, and each later page costs $4 plus $4. A county can tack on a preservation surcharge of up to $5 a document, so ask the recorder whether Darke County collects it and how much.

The same statute prices copies. Per page, a certified copy runs a $1 base fee plus a $1 housing trust fund fee, a recorder's seal on the certification adds $0.50 and $0.50, and a marginal reference entered through a separate instrument costs $2 and $2. Charges fall due when the paper is presented, and each page, caption page included, counts at its 8.5 by 14 inch size or fraction of one.

The seller. ORC 319.202(D) puts the conveyance fee under section 319.54(G)(3) on the grantor, along with any transfer tax the commissioners adopted under Chapter 322. The ceiling on a county transfer tax is thirty cents per hundred dollars of value, payable to the auditor ahead of recording (ORC 322.02). Ask the Darke County auditor whether one is in place.

On a sale, value is the entire price paid or payable, including any mortgage or vendor's lien. For a gift it means the likely open-market price, and willful falsification is prohibited. The auditor's site has a calculator that takes a parcel count and a sale price and includes the parcel transfer fee, so run your numbers before closing.

sections.h2: What the auditor checks on a deed
sections.html:
The stamp tells the recorder the paperwork is complete. Under ORC 319.202 the buyer, or someone acting for the buyer, files the value statement. The auditor then marks the deed with the fee and compliance, keeps the original, and sends the tax commissioner a copy noting the latest assessed value.

Two sets of affirmations ride on that statement. One asks about a homestead or owner-occupancy reduction taken on this year's or last year's tax. The other covers agricultural valuation. If either answer is yes, both sides sign a sworn instrument accounting for the reduction or the recoupment charge. For residential rental property, the indorsement also reminds the buyer of landlord information due under ORC 5323.02.

A family transfer or other exempt deed only needs the reason for the exemption. Pick the exempt form (DTE 100EX) and state the reason plainly.

sections.h2: What to expect on filing day
sections.html:
If the paperwork is in order, the visit is short. The auditor reviews the statement, takes the conveyance fee and any county transfer tax, and stamps the deed. You then walk the stamped deed to the recorder, who charges the page-based fee and records the instrument. Ask whether the office wants cash, a check or both, since each office collects its own payment.

Mortgage releases follow a different path. The recorder only records a release, and the lender is the party that files it, so a seller with a paid-off loan should ask the lender to confirm it was recorded. When the deed comes back, store it with your sale file, because the recorded copy proves that title passed to the buyer.

sections.h2: Searching Darke County land records online
sections.html:
The recorder's online search of land records begins at May 1996, and the office has been extending the index back to January 1980. Call to ask how far back it runs now and how to view older books in person.

A free Property Fraud Alert subscription warns an owner when a document is recorded against the property, a useful safeguard for anyone with an empty house.

  • Parcel searches, the county map and the sales report live on the auditor's website, not at the recorder.
  • Questions about value or tax on a parcel go to the auditor. Questions about what is already of record go to the recorder.

sections.h2: Land in Darke County: what a seller should know
sections.html:
The 2020 count was 51,881 residents. Land that families have held for decades makes the legal description important, and the county engineer reviews deeds for proper boundary descriptions. Cities, villages and townships hold zoning authority for their own ground, and a house in an unzoned township answers to the township trustees, so confirm that before you list. The parcel record shows the school district for tax purposes.

A tidy deed package saves time. Before you go, compare the legal description with your last deed, get any tax payoff from the treasurer, and have your lender record a release of an old mortgage. A cash buyer can close quickly, but the stamp and the filing still follow the same order: engineer, auditor, then recorder.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Darke County Recorder?
faqs.a: Call 937-547-7390 or go to the courthouse at 504 S. Broadway in Greenville. The office is open weekdays.

faqs.q: Is the Darke County filing charge based on page count?
faqs.a: Yes. Ohio sets one price for the first two pages and a lower price per added page, and a preservation surcharge of up to $5 may apply on top. ORC 317.32 has the list.

faqs.q: Which comes first in Darke County, auditor or recorder?
faqs.a: The auditor. The conveyance fee statement and fee earn the stamp, and the recorder then files the stamped deed.

faqs.q: Is a homemade deed acceptable in Darke County?
faqs.a: It can be brought in, but it needs a signature, an acknowledgment before an authorized official, a description the engineer's tax maps support and the auditor's stamp. A title company or attorney can prepare it.

faqs.q: Can older Darke County deeds be found online?
faqs.a: Online search starts with May 1996, and the office has been extending the index to January 1980. Ask what year it begins now.
